title_en: 위해(서) -- 'for the sake of / in order to'
summary_en: Names a beneficiary (N을 위해) or a purpose (-기 위해): for someone, or in order to do something.
ja_diff_note: Covers ために's benefit and purpose uses, but not its cause use: 雨のために中止 is 비 때문에, never 비를 위해. Purpose needs the -기 form of a verb, and in casual speech -(으)려고 is far more common, so 위해 sounds a bit earnest.
notes: N + 을/를 + 위해(서) (위하다 takes an object): 가족을 위해, 너를 위해서.
Before a noun: N을 위한 N: 엄마를 위한 선물.
Verb stem + 기 위해(서): 한국어를 배우기 위해. For adjectives, first make a verb: 건강해지기 위해.
Cause or reason is 때문에. Everyday purpose is often -(으)려고: 살 빼려고 걸어요.

examples.ko: 어머님을 위해서 일본 과자를 사 왔어요.
examples.en: I brought some Japanese snacks for you, Mother.
examples.ja: お母さんのために日本のお菓子を買ってきました。

examples.ko: 이선은 할머니하고 이야기하기 위해서 높임말을 연습해요.
examples.en: Ethan practices honorific speech so he can talk with Grandma.
examples.ja: イーサンはおばあちゃんと話すために敬語を練習しています。

drills.prompt_en: Father worked hard his whole life for the family.
drills.explain_en: 위하다 is transitive, so the beneficiary takes the object particle 을/를.

drills.prompt_en: I watch dramas in order to learn Korean.
drills.explain_en: Purpose is verb stem + 기 위해(서); the modifier -는 doesn't attach to 위해.

drills.prompt_en: We couldn't go on the picnic because of the rain.
drills.explain_en: Cause is 때문에; unlike ために, 위해 never expresses a reason.

drills.prompt_en: This is a present for Seoyun.
drills.explain_en: Directly before a noun (선물) you need the modifier form 를 위한.
